correctness.rationale: The explicit degree-three incidence inequality yields k>=8 with all equality constraints. A complete exhaustive C++17 classifier independently checks all sum_{i=0}^8 binomial(24,i)=1271626 vertex subsets (including all 735471 eight-sets), finds exactly eighteen and matches the A/B formulas. A separate Python checker enumerates 245025 four-outer/four-inner subsets and checks the full 153-pair overlap distribution, structure of the two eight-cycles, a graph automorphism joining families, the exact 3C6 exchange graph at budget four and ten-regular diameter-two graph at budget five. Both bundled source files were executed from their actual package paths with claimed output. The finite-search domain is exhaustive for the fixed graph; no claim of all-orders generalization or impossible extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact list of eighteen ordinary minimum LD sets in GP(12,5), their two eight-cycle sensor-incidence cores, one full symmetry orbit, complete optimum-overlap spectrum and a sharp batch exchange transition at five sensors. The known cubic lower bound and abstract reconfiguration framework are excluded from claims of novelty. Actual indexed searches and directly relevant full-text portions of the general regular-graph, generalized Petersen LD, and sensor-reconfiguration papers found no stronger result implying the conjunction. Publication priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Unindexed or non-digitized Nauru locating-code tables may exist.

A prior stronger arbitrary-cubic code classification may imply the finite statement even if it uses different terminology.
Independent external proof and publication-priority audit have not been performed.

value.rationale: The 24-vertex Nauru graph is a canonical cubic symmetric network, and minimum locating-dominating codes are a natural exact sensor-placement invariant. The new classification refines the known minimum-size lower bound into an entire eighteen-state optimal landscape, a two-C8 local incidence geometry, and a sharp four-versus-five replacement mobility transition. The precise value answers whether an optimal code can be relocated with limited simultaneous replacements; it is not a trivial bound renaming or arbitrary slice of unrelated parameters.
